title: Proof
body_md:
Using that $\pi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x)^{-1})v = \overline{\xi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x))}v$, we find that
 
\begin{align*}
 
\pi(\widetilde{s}(g.x))v &= \pi(\widetilde{s}(b(g).x) \widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x)) \widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x)^{-1})v \\
 
&= \pi(\widetilde{s}(b(g).x) \widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x))\pi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x)^{-1})v \\
 
&= \overline{\xi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x))} \pi(b(g)\widetilde{s}(x))v \\
 
&= \overline{\xi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x))} \pi(b(g)) \pi(\widetilde{s}(x))v 
 
\end{align*}
 
from which it follows that 
 
\begin{align*}
 
L(g.x_1, g.x_2) &= \langle \pi(\widetilde{s}(g.x_1))v, \pi(\widetilde{s}(g.x_2))v \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} \\
 
&= \overline{\xi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x_1))} \xi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x_2)) \langle \pi(b(g)) \pi(\widetilde{s}(x_1))v, \pi(b(g)) \pi(\widetilde{s}(x_2))v \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} \\
 
&= \overline{\xi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x_1))} \xi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x_2)) \langle \pi(\widetilde{s}(x_1))v, \pi(\widetilde{s}(x_2))v \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} \\
 
&= \overline{\xi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x_1))} \xi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x_2)) L(x_1, x_2) \, . 
 
\end{align*}
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: We emphasize that although $\widetilde{\gamma}_s$ is a cocycle, the map $c(g, x) = \overline{\xi(\widetilde{\gamma}_s(b(g), x))}$ is in general not, but only equivalent to a cocycle modulo some $2$-cocycle.
